_comment: Washington has no state income tax on wages. Employee payroll premiums (2026, verified 2026-10-10 on paidleave.wa.gov): Paid Family and Medical Leave 1.13% of wages up to the Social Security cap, employee share up to 71.43%; WA Cares 0.58% of all wages, no cap.
name: Washington
notes: Washington doesn't tax wages. Its capital gains tax only reaches high earners selling investments, not your paycheck.

Washington does take two small payroll premiums that other no-tax states don't. Paid Family and Medical Leave is 1.13% of wages in 2026, and employees pay up to 71.43% of it (about 0.81% of pay, up to $184,500 of wages). WA Cares, the long-term care program, is 0.58% of all wages. Both are included in the result above.
Some people are exempt from WA Cares, for example those who got an approved exemption for private long-term care insurance. If that's you, your check is about 0.58% bigger.
